verdict: The copy is tight, honest and sounds like X: the H1, 'Say it at 11 PM. Post it at 8:40 AM.', the Never list and the pricing lines are best-in-class, and every headline holds two lines at 1440 and 390 (9.99 screens at 390, 9.19 at 360, no horizontal scroll). It stops short of 9.5 because the engine's explanation copy is weaker than the page copy around it, most visibly in the closing section, where the proof example is a one-word cut explained by a stock line under a 'Why it hits' label.
to_95: Swap the closing-section example for a multi-cut line with a specific reason (e.g. the 'so i just wanted to say that our churn dropped 34%' class of edit, which the engine explains well: 'the line opens on ...'), so the last proof before the final CTA is the strongest edit on the page, not the weakest.

For single filler-word cuts, label the note 'What changed' everywhere (it already does this for 'honestly' but says 'Why it hits' for 'really' and 'literally') and rewrite the stock line '"X" was talk, not the point. The line says the same without it.' to something plainer such as 'Cut "literally". The number does the work.'
Stop the run-up note quoting the whole output line: quote the first three or four words only ('...so the line starts on "We just closed"').
Add 'a month' to the desktop Pro add-on line so it matches the phone version.

issues.where: Final CTA panel ('Good ideas die in bad first lines.'), right-hand example; same string appears in the Try box for one-word cuts
issues.problem: The last proof a visitor sees is the weakest edit on the page: 'my trading newsletter literally just hit 20,000 subscribers' loses one word, and the note under 'Why it hits' reads '"literally" was talk, not the point. The line says the same without it.' That sentence explains what was removed, not why the line hits, and 'was talk, not the point' is awkward phrasing. Next to the Try-box default ('it reads as your rule, not advice') it feels generic, and it lands right before the final ask.
issues.fix: Use a closing example with two or more cuts and a point-first result, with a specific reason line (the engine already writes these well: '"so" and "i just wanted to say that" went, so the line opens on "our churn dropped 34%"'). For any one-word filler cut, title the note 'What changed' and replace the stock sentence with a plain one, e.g. 'Cut "literally". The number does the work.'

issues.where: Try box, note heading after Sharpen
issues.problem: The heading is inconsistent for the same kind of edit: cutting 'honestly' shows 'What changed', cutting 'really' or 'literally' shows 'Why it hits'. 'Why it hits' over a one-word removal overclaims.
issues.fix: Rule: 'Why it hits' only when the note names an effect on the reader (beat, point first, rule not advice); otherwise 'What changed'.

issues.where: Try box, input "I'm thrilled to announce that we just closed our $2M seed round led by Acme"
issues.problem: The note quotes the entire output back: 'The run-up is gone, so the line starts on "We just closed our $2M seed round led by Acme".' It reads as filler on a product that sells cutting filler.
issues.fix: Quote only the opening words, up to the first number or four words: 'The run-up is gone, so the line starts on "We just closed our $2M".'

issues.where: Try box summary row, e.g. 'Cut 1 bit of fluff · Split it into two beats · Left a reason to read on · 1 left to you'
issues.problem: '1 left to you' is cryptic on first read, and four chips in a row is more than the eye takes in; the explanation ('Left "i think" in: it marks this as your view') is already below.
issues.fix: Cap the row at two or three items and reword the last to '1 your call' or drop it, since the note below already says it.

issues.where: Pro card at 1440: 'Need more? +250 for $8, +750 for $22 or +1,750 for $45.'
issues.problem: No period stated on desktop, so it can be read as a one-off top-up; the 390 version correctly says '+250 for $8 a month'.
issues.fix: Desktop: 'Need more? +250 for $8 a month, +750 for $22 or +1,750 for $45.'

issues.where: Under the plan cards: 'A rewrite is three takes on a line. Reply drafts you ask for: ten count as one. Reply-ping drafts are free.'
issues.problem: Three accounting rules in three clipped sentences; 'ten count as one' needs a second read to learn the unit (one rewrite).
issues.fix: 'One rewrite gives you three takes on a line. Ten reply drafts you ask for use one rewrite. Reply-ping drafts are free.'
